0	\section{Introduction}
1	\label{sec:introduction}
2	
3	World-model reinforcement learning enables sample-efficient learning directly on physical hardware \citep{wu2023daydreamer, hansen2024tdmpc2}. Real robotic tasks demand temporal abstraction: manipulation requires fast reactive grasping alongside slow approach planning, locomotion involves gait phases at different frequencies, and sim-to-real transfer must handle $\dt$ mismatches between simulation and hardware. TAWM \citep{nhu2025tawm} shows that conditioning a world model on step size $\dt$ yields consistent gains within TD-MPC2's MPC framework \citep{hansen2024tdmpc2}. Can the same $\dt$-conditioning bring temporal abstraction to imagination-based actor-critic methods like DreamerV3 \citep{hafner2023dreamerv3}, where policies are trained entirely in imagined rollouts?
4	
5	We find that it cannot. Every variable-rate configuration degrades performance catastrophically (14--19\% of baseline). Through a factorial analysis on Walker Walk \citep{tassa2018dmcontrol}, we isolate the combination of a \emph{trained} $\dt$-embedding and multi-rate data exposure as the strongest predictor. This combination enables the RSSM reward head to develop a $2.78\times$ prediction gap between $\dt{=}1$ and $\dt{=}2$, which the critic internalizes as optimistic value estimates, a failure mode we term \emph{conditioning-induced value overestimation} (CIVO), analogous to delusional bias \citep{lu2018nondelusional} but model-induced rather than policy-class-induced. A normalized value-to-eval (NVE) threshold of $\geq 1.5\times$ achieves 26/29 classification ($n{=}29$, two environments, AUROC${=}0.953$, in-sample; LOEO cross-validated, Appendix~Table~\ref{tab:nve_loeo}).
6	
7	Gradient decomposition reveals that gradient magnitude does not predict causal importance: the reward head contributes 38--49\% of $\nabla_\theta e_{\dt}$ yet reward-only stopping fails, while the observation decoder (16--22\%) carries the critical signal. A four-level intervention hierarchy (gradient, output, representation, architecture) shows that no tested intervention reliably eliminates CIVO across environments. In pure-imagination training, dual critics converge to identical value functions ($\rho > 0.999$), rendering Double Q pessimism ineffective; the min operation nonetheless enables CIVO recovery, while prevention requires min $+$ increased capacity. These findings are directly relevant to robotics: as world-model RL moves toward real systems with variable-rate sensing and multi-timescale control, understanding when temporal conditioning fails, and why standard countermeasures cannot fix it, is essential for safe deployment.
8	
9	\paragraph{Contributions.}
10	\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
11	    \item \textbf{Failure mode identification.} We identify CIVO as specific to imagination-based actor-critic with temporal conditioning and isolate trained $\dt$-embedding $+$ multi-rate exposure as jointly sufficient in tested configurations (6/6 seeds, two locomotion environments, AUROC${=}0.953$, in-sample; LOEO cross-validated). Cross-environment validation spanning locomotion and manipulation (ManiSkill) establishes that CIVO is locomotion-specific; frozen-embedding controls on three manipulation tasks identify value-ratio transients as environment-driven, demonstrating the diagnostic's specificity on non-CIVO dynamics.
12	    \item \textbf{Architectural boundary.} $\dt$-conditioning succeeds in TD-MPC2's MPC re-planning but fails under imagination-based bootstrapping, where model errors compound into biased value targets with no real-data anchor.
13	    \item \textbf{Four-level intervention hierarchy.} Across gradient, output, representation, and architecture levels, no intervention reliably eliminates CIVO across environments. Gradient magnitude does not predict causal importance (reward head: 38--49\%, reward-only stopping fails). In pure-imagination training, dual critics converge ($\rho > 0.999$), eliminating Double Q pessimism, though the min operation enables recovery through a different mechanism.
14	    \item \textbf{Online detection.} A lightweight NVE-based detector achieves 100\% sensitivity (5/5) with predictive warning in 2/5 cases.
15	\end{enumerate}

641	\citet{nhu2025tawm} show that $\dt$-conditioning benefits TD-MPC2, raising the question of why it fails in DreamerV3.  The critical difference is that MPC re-plans from real states at every step, so imagination errors do not accumulate into the training signal because there is no critic bootstrapping from imagined trajectories.  In DreamerV3, the actor-critic trains entirely within imagination, and any systematic reward-prediction bias at $\dt > 1$ is amplified through the closed actor-critic loop.
642	
643	\subsection{The \texorpdfstring{$\dt$}{dt}-Embedding Dilemma}
644	\label{sec:embedding_dilemma}
645	
646	The factorial results reveal a fundamental tension: removing the $\dt$-embedding (008f) eliminates CIVO but at a $13\times$ cost to reward prediction quality ($0.7469$ vs.\ $0.0568$ MAE), as the world model cannot distinguish temporal scales.  Restricting imagination to $\dt{=}1$ while retaining the trained embedding (008e\_v3) avoids collapse in 2 of 4 seeds (50\%), while the remaining two collapse via distinct mechanisms: Pathway~A (CIVO-driven, entropy decrease; s3, NVE $4.02\times$) and Pathway~B (entropy-driven, entropy increase; s2, NVE $3.78\times$; \S\ref{sec:f6}).  Neither approach alone provides a complete solution.
647	
648	\subsection{Multiple Vulnerability Pathways}
649	\label{sec:pathways}
650	
651	The two collapse patterns identified in \S\ref{sec:f6}---CIVO (Pathway~A, value-driven, entropy decreasing) and a tentative second mode (Pathway~B, eval-driven, entropy increasing)---have distinct diagnostic signatures. Pathway~B is observed in only two seeds (008e\_v3\_s2 and 038\_s2); we present it as preliminary evidence that the trained $\dt$-embedding's learned features may affect both reward prediction across temporal scales (Pathway~A) and the representation space in which the actor operates (Pathway~B), though additional data is needed to confirm this as a distinct mechanism.  This explains why $\nve$ is sensitive but not perfectly specific: Pathway~B's late evaluation decline inflates $\nve$ through the same arithmetic as CIVO, yielding the sole false positive ($3.78\times$ for 008e\_v3 s2). All three produce NVE $> 1.5\times$ through non-CIVO mechanisms, indicating that the NVE diagnostic detects value overestimation broadly rather than CIVO specifically---a feature rather than a limitation for practitioners monitoring deployment health. The closest sub-threshold case (008f seed~4, NVE${=}1.41\times$) lacks $\dt$-conditioning entirely ($d{=}0$); its elevated NVE reflects transient value noise that self-corrects without the positive feedback loop characteristic of CIVO. The closest above-threshold positive (008d seed~3, NVE${=}1.53\times$) exhibits the full CIVO causal chain: trained $\dt$-embedding, entropy decrease, and evaluation collapse to 14\% of baseline.

242	\subsection{NVE Normalization Robustness}
243	\label{sec:nve_robustness}

245	To assess sensitivity to baseline seed choice, we extend the single-seed baseline (seed~1, eval 915.7 at 105K) to three additional seeds trained to 505K steps (Table~\ref{tab:baseline_seeds}).

378	
379	The empirical finding that trained embedding \emph{plus} multi-rate exposure jointly predict CIVO rests on two complementary controls that each remove one factor while holding the other constant.
380	
381	\paragraph{Evidence A: exposure is necessary (exp\_008a).}
382	Exp\_008a uses a trained embedding ($d{=}32$, gradients enabled) that is never exposed to $\dt{>}1$ transitions during world-model training (subsample OFF). Despite sharing the same embedding architecture as exp\_008d, its NVE remains in the $0.83$--$0.93\times$ range across 3 seeds (105K steps). Performance follows two V-shaped recovery cycles, reaching 777.7 at 105K (85\% of baseline). The critical factor is not the embedding's capacity to represent temporal information, but its adaptation to multi-rate data that enables precise but inaccurate $\dt{>}1$ state predictions within the RSSM.
383	
384	This contrasts with exp\_006 (trained $e_{\dt}$, subsample ON, $H{=}15$), where NVE accelerates from $1.61\times$ at 45K to $2.31\times$ at 55K before catastrophic collapse to 132.9 at 65K. Both experiments use identical trained embeddings ($d{=}32$, gradients enabled) and $H{=}15$, differing only in whether the world model sees $\dt{>}1$ transitions during training. This confirms that multi-rate data exposure, not embedding architecture, is the operative variable.
385	
386	\paragraph{Evidence B: trainability is necessary (exp\_015b).}
387	Exp\_015b uses a frozen random-projection embedding ($d{=}32$, \texttt{requires\_grad=False}, subsample ON, $H{=}8$), the same multi-rate data regime as exp\_008d, but with a non-trainable temporal signal.
